courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: Now one important note about our map.
Now we're making good progress,
next maps will be to use our address for all the places where we output our places
but before we do that, let's have a look at the map modal again
and there, we have one issue right now. I'm setting up that listener here
and actually, we never cleared that listener for clicks on the map when we dismissed the modal.
It's not a huge problem here but it could introduce a memory leak,
so we want to make sure we do clean this up.
So let me add onDestroy here to be forced to add the ngOnDestroy method like this
and now with ngOnDestroy added, when I add my listener here, this actually returns me a handle to
that listener which I can store in a property, click listener for example would be a name I can choose.
So this click listener is equal to map add listener, this returns me a reference to that listener and
then in ngOnDestroy,
we can now remove that listener with the help of that Google Maps object here, so therefore let's store
this in a global variable as well,
Google Maps of type any and in here, I will set this Google Map,
so this property equal to Google Maps I get as an argument here and then now here, we can use both, we can
use this Google Maps or just Google Maps, whatever you prefer but down there in ngOnDestroy, we
can now use this Google Maps.event remove listener and then this click listener and this should
ensure that when we dismiss the modal and therefore clear the map, we actually get rid of that click
listener
so that we don't introduce a memory leak, yes.
And this looks good,
it still works as before as you can tell
but now behind the scenes, this is in a bit of a more optimal state.
